newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM BEATEN INTO THIRD IN ECLIPSE STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM BEATEN INTO THIRD IN ECLIPSE STAKES.

text.p: Bosra Sham, the filly who looked a world-beater at Royal Ascot just over two weeks ago, was beaten into third place in the Eclipse Stakes at Sandown Park on Saturday.

Despite a small field, jockey Kieren Fallon, riding the hot favourite for trainer Henry Cecil, found himself checked early in the straight and failed to peg back Pilsudski, the mount of Michael Kinane and Epsom Derby winner Benny The Dip, ridden by Willie Ryan.
Pilsudski, the Breeders' Cup Turf winner last year, triumphed by one and a quarter lengths with a short head separating second and third.

Bosra Sham, the 7-4 on favourite, travelled well enough in the 10-furlong (2-km) group one event, but when she went for a gap on the rails at a critical stage, pacesetting Benny The Dip (6-1) blocked her run.
Pilsudski, an 11-2 chance, battled clear to land the $245,000 spoils and offer handsome compensation for a surprise defeat on the final day of Royal Ascot 15 days ago.
Winning trainer Michael Stoute said: "We didn't quite get it right at Ascot but I think we got it right today."
Kinane, who has a host of major international race victories to his credit, said: "I was not in awe of Bosra Sham because I was happy with my horse at Ascot."
Only five horses contested the race, with many trainers wary of taking on Bosra Sham, rated by Cecil after a stunning eight length Ascot victory as the best horse he has ever trained.
